deep_dive.title: Motion-Based Tokenization for Cross-Dataset Egocentric Gaze Modeling
deep_dive.abstract: Gaze is increasingly used as an input signal for vision and multimodal models, yet no consensus exists on how to represent it across datasets. Raw traces preserve detail but are noisy and device-dependent, while coarse event labels are easy to model but can discard local motion structure. We formulate event-aligned, fixed-horizon angular displacement as an interpretable, event-conditioned motion vocabulary and compare it with event-only, spatial, absolute-angle, learned vector-quantized, and continuous representations. To assess transfer alongside target predictability and token collapse, our evaluation combines next-token prediction with target-domain regret, low-order target references, paired bootstrap, order sensitivity, motif overlap, and frozen structural probes. In an event-aligned headset benchmark, angular-motion tokens have lower target-domain regret than frozen-codebook VQ tokens in one transfer direction, while the reverse direction is inconclusive. The probes reveal complementary representation properties, and event-only tokens show that low perplexity can retain little motion information. On a third egocentric dataset, a matched comparison of I-VT, native, and frame-span interfaces shows that event construction materially changes transfer: native events have the lowest regret into EGTEA, while frame-span events have zero motif overlap and fail severely as a source. Motion-based tokenization therefore provides a compact representation for event-aligned egocentric gaze streams, while the evaluation identifies how target predictability and event construction shape cross-dataset conclusions.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_en: This paper proposes motion-based tokenization for egocentric gaze, using event-aligned angular displacement as an interpretable event-conditioned motion vocabulary, evaluated across datasets; provides a reusable gaze representation for multimodal intent prediction.
deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 针对眼动追踪数据在跨数据集中缺乏统一表示的问题，该论文提出基于运动的令牌化方法，将事件对齐的固定时间窗角位移定义为可解释的、以事件为条件的运动词汇，并与多种表示进行对比。评估结合下一令牌预测、目标域遗憾值等多项指标，验证了该表示在迁移性和目标可预测性上的优势。该方法为多模态模型提供了统一而有效的视线输入表示，有助于视线驱动的意图预测和人机交互。
